expect.note: not_a_dump's ratio must be judged against the real page (body_len), not the stored evidence window -- so the SAME value read from the SAME page must not flip verdict depending only on whether the plan carried a distant anchor that forces evidence_window() to append a second window

provenance: reviewer-reported, reproduced: verifier.py divided len(clean(value)) by len(clean(page_text)), but page_text is evidence_window()'s output -- a storage artifact capped at PAGE_TEXT_KEEP and doubled (agent.py:171-173) when a distant anchor forces a second window onto it. Watched red before the fix: a 776-char value on a body whose plain window is 2000 chars gave ratio 0.388 (FAIL, not_a_dump=False); the SAME value and body with a distant anchor gave a 3615-char window, ratio 0.2147 (PASS, not_a_dump=True) -- same value, same page, opposite verdict, decided by nothing but whether the plan happened to carry an anchor. The true page fraction (776/4388 ~= 0.177) is well under DUMP_RATIO and was never a dump either way.

triage.note: the fix records body_len (len(body) at extraction time, which agent.py already has in hand) alongside value/page_text, and verify() prefers it over len(clean(page_text)) for the not_a_dump denominator, falling back to the window length when body_len is absent -- which is every one of the 25 frozen records in evals/labels/verifier-sample.jsonl, so their replay is unchanged by design (specs/decisions/ADR-008-m7-verifier-accuracy.md).
